metadata.source: Derived, rule-based layer computed entirely from this portal's own already-published pipeline outputs -- climate indices (ERA5-Land (ECMWF) + CHIRPS (UCSB), via Google Earth Engine, 2000-2024), NDVI (UNDP DiCRA or MODIS/GEE, where available), soil moisture (NASA SMAP L4/GEE, where available). NOT a machine-learning model, NOT a probability/confidence score -- every flag is a fixed, code-defined threshold rule. See docs/METHODOLOGY.md Sec 9 for the exact rules; scripts/15_build_advisory.py is the reference implementation.
metadata.method: Rule-based thresholds on real stored values; see each flag's own 'basis'/'note' for the exact source field(s) and threshold used.
metadata.data_quality: derived (rule-based, not independently measured) -- see 'source' for the real underlying pipeline output each flag traces to
metadata.processing: Rule-based thresholds on real stored values; see each flag's own 'basis'/'note' for the exact source field(s) and threshold used.

heatwave_risk.note: 2.44 heatwave days/yr and 0.08 severe heatwave days/yr (2000-2024 mean, ERA5-Land (ECMWF) + CHIRPS (UCSB), via Google Earth Engine, 2000-2024). Threshold: severe_heatwave_days>=2 -> EXTREME, heatwave_days>=8 -> HIGH, >=2 -> MODERATE, else LOW (same bands as the district climate panel).

drought_risk.note: drought_probability_pct=16.8%, spi_12=0.00 (2000-2024, ERA5-Land (ECMWF) + CHIRPS (UCSB), via Google Earth Engine, 2000-2024). Below both threshold bands -> LOW.

basis.observation_window: 2026-08-07T11:08Z to 2026-08-12T11:08Z (3-hourly SMAP L4 images, averaged per grid cell over this window)

irrigation_need.note: sm_surface_mean=0.239 m3/m3 (0-5cm), sm_rootzone_mean=0.218 m3/m3 (0-100cm), N=38 SMAP cells, window 2026-08-07T11:08Z to 2026-08-12T11:08Z (3-hourly SMAP L4 images, averaged per grid cell over this window). Threshold (same as the Soil Moisture tab): <0.15 -> HIGH (irrigate soon), <0.30 -> MODERATE, else LOW. No per-district soil-moisture time series is stored yet (SMAP pipeline keeps a current ~5-day window only), so this is the fixed reference band, not a trend.
